name: device-cdac-cap
description: CDAC unit-capacitor characterization: MiM (2.0 / 1.0 fF/um^2) and 3.3 V MOS cap, effective C at 1 MHz over the cap corners.
claim: None yet — device characterization ahead of a ratified spec line (#1). Also the harness's proof that the mimcap/moscap .lib sections take effect, which no MOS-only corner sweep can show.

cmim_2f0_ff.description: 10x10 um MiM at 2.0 fF/um^2 is ~200 fF plus perimeter. The process floor proves the mimcap_ff/mimcap_ss sections are actually selected — the guard a MOS-only sweep cannot provide.

cmim_1f0_ff.description: same geometry at 1.0 fF/um^2. Independent confirmation the MiM corner params reach both density flavors.

cmos_ff.description: 3.3 V NMOS cap biased at vdd. The process floor proves moscap_ff/moscap_ss take effect; the supply floor exercises the device's voltage coefficient, which is why a MOS cap is a poor CDAC unit element.

cmim_density_ratio.description: the 2.0 fF/um^2 flavor holds ~2x the 1.0 fF/um^2 flavor at equal area; a sanity check that both aliases resolve to different models.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated — gf180mcu ngspice device models (sm141064_mim.ngspice cap_mim_new, sm141064.ngspice moscap), swept over the PDK's own mimcap/moscap corner sections. No foundry datasheet or literature value is involved.
notes: Effective C is derived from a 1 A AC probe at 1 MHz: C = 1/(2*pi*f*|V|). It is a small-signal capacitance at the stated bias, not a large-signal charge-transfer capacitance.
The open gf180mcu PDK ships no MoM / lateral-flux capacitor model, so no MoM corner is swept here; a MoM-based CDAC would need parasitic extraction rather than a model corner.
